question: The grammar of the effect language: CEffect::LoadKey's default branch, the slot-7 scalar handlers, the block effects' keys and value forms.

addresses.name: CEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CEffect::LoadKey(CEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The effect half of the event script language**, inherited by 74 effect classes, and the loader every block of child effects is read through. One switch over the key's save token with **91 cases**; most constructors are inlined, some are calls. `kill_leader` is case 1532, `CKillLeaderEffect` - the one BiceLib's Hooks/EffectText hangs a tooltip on. The keyword table is in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md, regenerated by `switchmap.py 0x999CA0`.

**Every case ends in one of two tails, and the tail - not the value written - decides the grammar.** 67 cases go to the scalar tail at 0x59A038 (0x99A038): link the new effect as a child of `this`, copy the **value** token (`parse +0x228`, 0x104 bytes) and call the child's **slot 7, TakeScalarValue**. 24 cases go to the block tail at 0x59A0C3: link it and call the child's **slot 3, Load**, which reads key/value pairs until `}`. Neither tail looks at the value's token type, so a scalar keyword written with a block, or a block keyword written with a scalar, is not refused - see FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md on what that does to the rest of the file.

**The default arm, 0x59B26B-0x59B61C, in this order** (key text from `parse +0x24`, all lookups exact and case-sensitive): (1) a government position, GetGovernmentPositions + CNameDataBase::GetByName -> CReplaceMinisterEffect, scalar (`head_of_state = 23050`); (2) a building, StringHashFind_At1C on the building database -> CBuildingEffect, scalar (`industry = 5`); (3) an ideology, GetIdeologies + GetByName -> CAllOrganisationPopularityEffect, **block** (`fascistic = { organisation = 5 popularity = 5 }`); (4) a technology, StringHashFind_At20C -> CTechnologyInvestmentEffect, scalar; (5) a rebel type, StringHashFind_AtC -> CCreateRebelsEffect, scalar; (6) a region, CMap_FindRegion -> CRegionScopeEffect, **block** (`limit` plus effects); (7) a sub-unit type, StringHashFind on CSubUnitDataBase -> CAddSubUnitEffect, scalar (`infantry_brigade = current`); (8) **if the value token is `{` (type 3)**, a CContextEffect over the key token, block - **with no check that the key is a scope**: a tag, a number or one of the nine scope words resolve at run time, anything else is a context that never resolves and whose children never run; (9) otherwise `Unknown effect-type '<key>' in <file>` through LogRecord, `effect.cpp` line 246 on channel 0x10004, and nothing is built. **ReportUnknownKey and ReportParseError are never called from this function** (0 call sites; 108 operator new sites found by the same scan).

Laws are not in the chain: `training_laws = x` as an effect is step 9. Corrects FINDINGS-script.md's 'a province id, an ideology, then the technology database', which does not describe this loader. The common tail at 0x59B625 writes the keyword's token into the new child's `+0x18`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole in a copy of the applied project and the default arm re-read in the disassembly (0x99B26B-0x99B647): the seven lookup calls and their constructors in the order given, `cmp dword ptr [ecx+0x228], 3` at 0x99B4C7 before the 0x130-byte CContextEffect, and the log at 0x99B587 with `push 0x10004; push 0xf6`. The two tails: the only [vftable+0x1C] dispatches are 0x99A057 and 0x99B32E, the only [vftable+0xC] ones 0x99A0E5/0x99A0FA/0x99B56B/0x99B580. Every block-tail class has its own LoadKey or Load and every scalar-tail class has its own slot 7 except CModifySpiesEffect (vtable.py over all 101 family tables). Wrong if a tail were found that tests parse+0x228.
addresses.revises: the default branch, the two tails and the 67/24 split are new; the comment's 'inlines its constructors' was too strong

addresses.name: CRelationEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRelationEffect::LoadKey(CRelationEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `relation = { who = <tag|THIS|FROM> value = <n> }`. **Two keys, not four**: `who` and `value`. `this` and `from` are compared against the **value** token of `who`, which is why definitions.py saw them in the switch. `who`: token `this` sets `use_this (+0x1C)`, `from` sets `use_from (+0x1D)`, anything else is CCountryDataBase::GetTag on the text into +0x20/+0x24 (`---`/0 for an unknown tag; only the first three characters are compared, case-insensitively). `value`: ParseFixedPoint into +0x28, so it takes up to three decimals and is stored in thousandths. A key it does not name is dropped in silence - and its value is not consumed, so a dropped key written with a block leaves that block to the enclosing loader (FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and read: `key == value` -> ParseFixedPoint(parse, this+0x28); `key == who` -> tests `(parse->value).type` against this/from, else GetTag. Wrong if a `from`/`this` key case were found that does not read the value token.
addresses.revises: the four keys were two keys plus two values of `who`

addresses.name: CMultipleTargetEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CMultipleTargetEffect::LoadKey(CMultipleTargetEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: The loader of the eleven iterating scopes - `any_country`, `any_owned`, `any_controlled`, `any_neighbor_country`, `any_neighbor_province`, `random_country`, `random_owned`, `random_neighbor_province`, `random_empty_neighbor_province`, and every **region name** (CRegionScopeEffect) - and of nothing else. `limit` calls slot 3 (Load) of the CAndTrigger embedded at +0x20, so a limit is a trigger block and several `limit` blocks all append to the one AND. **Every other key goes to CEffect::LoadKey**, so it becomes a child effect: this is how the scope's effects are read, and nothing here is dropped.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: `if (key != limit) CEffect::LoadKey(this, parse, key); else (*(this+0x20)->vftable[3])(parse)`. CMultipleTargetEffect::CMultipleTargetEffect (0x59C320) writes CTrigger's and then CAndTrigger's vftable at +0x20. Wrong if a key besides `limit` were handled before the fallback.
addresses.revises: the generic 'anything else is dropped in silence' was wrong: everything else is a child effect

addresses.name: CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect::LoadKey(CAnyNearbyProvinceEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `any_nearby_province = { distance = <int> limit = { ... } <effects> }`. `distance` is `sscanf("%i")` into +0x60 - an integer, in map units - and a value that does not start with a number queues ReportParseError. `limit` is the embedded CAndTrigger's Load, as in CMultipleTargetEffect. **Every other key goes to CEffect::LoadKey** and becomes a child effect.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: distance -> sscanf(value.text, "%i" (0x15FD14C), this+0x60) with ReportParseError on 0; limit -> this+0x20 slot 3; else CEffect::LoadKey. The format string read out of the image.
addresses.revises: unknown keys are child effects, not dropped; distance is %i

addresses.name: CRandomEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRandomEffect::LoadKey(CRandomEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `random = { chance = <int> <effects> }`. `chance` is `atoi(text) * 1000` into +0x20 - a whole percentage, decimals truncated before the multiply. **Every other key goes to CEffect::LoadKey** and becomes a child effect run when the roll passes (CRandomEffect::Execute).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: `if (key != chance) CEffect::LoadKey(...); else this+0x20 = atoi(value.text) * 1000`. Wrong if chance were read through ParseFixedPoint.
addresses.revises: unknown keys are child effects, not dropped

addresses.name: CPracticalEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CPracticalEffect::LoadKey(CPracticalEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **The two keys of the `practical` effect.** `technology_group` (530) reads a string and looks it up as a technology **category** in the technology database's map at +0x2C - the names common/technology.txt lists - keeping it at the effect's +0x20 only when the object's slot 2 answers true; `value` (678) goes through ParseFixedPoint into +0x24. Because the text tokenizer's slot 2 answers false (rva 0x192360 is `xor al, al; ret`), that number always takes the scaling path, so it is thousandths and `value = 5` means five levels. **Every other key goes to CEffect::LoadKey** and is parsed as a child effect; whether CPracticalEffect::Execute runs children was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md and FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: `if (key != technology_group) { if (key != value) CEffect::LoadKey(...); else ParseFixedPoint(parse, this+0x24); }`. Wrong if the fallback call were absent in the bytes.
addresses.revises: 'Anything else is dropped' was wrong: anything else is a child effect

addresses.name: CWarEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CWarEffect::LoadKey(CWarEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `war = { target = <tag|THIS|FROM> call_ally = yes|no limited = yes|no attacker_goal = { ... } defender_goal = { ... } }`. **Five keys, not seven**: `this` and `from` are values of `target` (use_this +0x1C / use_from +0x1D; else GetTag into +0x20/+0x24). `call_ally` is a **case-insensitive** `_stricmp` against `yes` and `no` into the byte at +0x48, any other text leaving it alone; `limited` is ParseBool into +0x49. `attacker_goal`/`defender_goal` each build a CWarGoal (0x479760), read it with its own Load (CWarGoal::LoadKey's keys) and append it (0x9BE8F0). **Every other key goes to CEffect::LoadKey** and is parsed as a child effect; whether CWarEffect::Execute runs children was not read.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole: the token compare of target's value against this/from, the two _stricmp calls on "yes"/"no", ParseBool(parse, this+0x49), and `goto LAB_009bc652` -> CEffect::LoadKey for anything else.
addresses.revises: this/from are values, not keys; unknown keys are child effects, not dropped

addresses.name: CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect::LoadKey(CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `undeclared_war = { target = <tag|THIS|FROM> region = <region name> }`. **Two keys, not four**: `this`/`from` are values of `target`. `region` is ParseString then the region table lookup StringHashFind_At18 (exact, case-sensitive) into +0x28; a miss logs `non-existent region '<name>'.` (effect.cpp line 0x11FD, channel 0x10004) and keeps the null. **Every other key goes to CEffect::LoadKey** as a child effect.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; the log call LogRecord::Make("effect.cpp", 0x11FD, 0x10004) and the fallback are both in the body.
addresses.revises: this/from are values; region misses are logged; unknown keys are child effects

addresses.name: CWarGoalEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CWarGoalEffect::LoadKey(CWarGoalEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `add_wargoal = { target = <tag|THIS|FROM> war_goal = { ... } }`. **Two keys, not four**: `this`/`from` are values of `target` (+0x1C/+0x1D, else GetTag into +0x20/+0x24). `war_goal` is slot 3 (Load) of the CWarGoal embedded at +0x28, so its block is CWarGoal::LoadKey's grammar. **Every other key goes to CEffect::LoadKey** as a child effect.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole. The constructor (0x5BD3F0) writes CWarGoal's vftable at +0x28.
addresses.revises: this/from are values, not keys; unknown keys are child effects

addresses.name: CModifySpiesEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CModifySpiesEffect::LoadKey(CModifySpiesEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **Dead code.** The keys are `target` (whose value may be a tag, `this` or `FROM`) and `value` (plain atoi into +0x28), everything else going to CEffect::LoadKey - and nothing ever calls this: `modify_spies` is built with the effect table's scalar tail, which calls slot 7 rather than Load. See CModifySpiesEffect::Execute and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: `this`/`from` are compared against target's value token, not against the key; the fallback is CEffect::LoadKey.
addresses.revises: there is no bare this/from key - they are values of target - and unknown keys fall to CEffect::LoadKey

addresses.name: CAllOrganisationPopularityEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAllOrganisationPopularityEffect::LoadKey(CAllOrganisationPopularityEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: The block an **ideology name** opens in an effect - `fascistic = { organisation = 5 popularity = 5 }`, CEffect::LoadKey's default arm step 3. **Two keys**: `organisation` (1224) into +0x28 and `popularity` (1275) into +0x2C, both through TokenToFixedPoint, so both take up to three decimals and are thousandths. A key it does not name is dropped in silence - and its value is not consumed, so a dropped key written with a block leaves that block to the enclosing loader (FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x9B8FB0-0x9B8FFB: `sub eax, 0x4c8; je` (organisation -> [esi+0x28]) then `sub eax, 0x33; jne` (popularity -> [esi+0x2C]). definitions.py's '1 key' missed the first arm of a sub/je chain.
addresses.revises: two keys, not one: organisation was missed

addresses.name: CThreatEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CThreatEffect::LoadKey(CThreatEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: `threat = { who = <tag|all> value = <int> }`. `who` and `which` are **the same key**: token `all` sets the byte at +0x2C, any other text is CCountryDataBase::GetTag into +0x24/+0x28 (`---`/0 when unknown). **There is no this/from form.** `value` is `atoi * 1000` into +0x20 - whole numbers only. A key it does not name is dropped in silence - and its value is not consumed, so a dropped key written with a block leaves that block to the enclosing loader (FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole: `if (key == value) ... atoi*1000; if (key == who || key == which) { if (value.type != all) GetTag(...) else this[0x2C] = 1 }`.
addresses.revises: adds the value forms: who/which equivalent, `all`, no this/from, integer value

addresses.name: CAddCountryModifierEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAddCountryModifierEffect::LoadKey(CAddCountryModifierEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: The loader of `add_country_modifier` and `add_province_modifier` (both CAddModifierEffect). **Two keys**: `name` looks the text up in the static-modifier database (CTraitDataBase_Find over g_static_modifiers - exact, case-sensitive) into +0x24, and a miss logs `Unknown modifier-type '<name>'.` (effect.cpp line 0x42B, channel 0x10004) and keeps the null; `duration` is plain `atoi` into +0x20 - days, whole numbers, **no x1000**. A key it does not name is dropped in silence - and its value is not consumed, so a dropped key written with a block leaves that block to the enclosing loader (FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; LogRecord::Make("effect.cpp", 0x42B, 0x10004) on a null lookup.
addresses.revises: adds the lookup, its log line and the value scales

addresses.name: CSetVariableEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CSetVariableEffect::LoadKey(CSetVariableEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: The loader of `set_variable` and `change_variable` (both CVariableEffect). **Two keys**: `which` assigns the value text to the Hoi3CString at +0x20 (no lookup - a variable is created by name), `value` is TokenToFixedPoint into +0x3C - up to three decimals, thousandths. A key it does not name is dropped in silence - and its value is not consumed, so a dropped key written with a block leaves that block to the enclosing loader (FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md).
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole.

addresses.name: CRandomListEffect::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRandomListEffect::LoadKey(CRandomListEffect* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: Its keys are the **weights** of a `random_list` - a key the lexer classed as a number (`tok_int`, 0xC), read with plain `atoi` (so `1.5` is 1, and no x1000). Each one adds to the total at +0x20, appends the weight to the CList<int> at +0x24, builds a bare CEffect (0x20 bytes, CEffect's own vftable) and calls its Load, so **the block under each weight is a block of child effects** read by CEffect::LoadKey; that effect is appended to this effect's own child list. Any other key - including `limit` - is dropped in silence without consuming its value.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole: `if (key == tok_int) { w = atoi(key.text); total += w; append w; e = new CEffect; e->Load(parse); append e }`, nothing else.
addresses.revises: adds what each weight's block is and what an unknown key does

addresses.name: CBoolEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `fixed_ai_strategy` and `form_government_in_exile`. Clears use_this/use_from; token `this` sets +0x1C and stores false; token `from` sets +0x1D and falls through; then `+0x20 = (token == yes)`. So **only the bare word `yes` (any case) is true** - `no`, a quoted "yes", a number and any other text are false, and `this`/`from` are always false. 0x59DC50 to `ret 0x104` at 0x59DC8D; CBoolEffect::FormatValueText follows at 0x59DC90.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and the ret read. Held at slot 7 by exactly CFixedAIStrategyEffect and CFormGovernmentInExileAction, the two CBoolEffect heirs - inheritance, not a fold.

addresses.name: CStringEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `load_oob` and `remove_brigade`. Clears use_this; `this`/`from` set +0x1C/+0x1D; and then **always** assigns the value text to CStringEffect::text (+0x20), `this` and `from` included. No lookup, so a load_oob file name or a regiment name is taken verbatim and only checked when the effect runs. `ret 0x104` at 0x59E218.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; ret read. Held by CLoadOOBEffect and CRemoveBrigadeEffect only, both CStringEffect heirs.

addresses.name: CAddCoreEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `add_core`, and **one value is read two ways at once**: `this`/`from` set +0x1C/+0x1D, otherwise CCountryDataBase::GetTag(text) into +0x20/+0x24; and in every case `atoi(text)` into +0x28. So `add_core = 1306` is province 1306 (the tag lookup on "130" finds nothing) and `add_core = SLO` is tag SLO with province 0. Execute (0x59FE40) then takes the province from +0x28, else the scope's province, and the country from the named tag, else the scope's - so a number adds the scope country's core to that province and a tag adds that country's core to the scope province. `add_core = from` means **the scope's FROM province** (scope +0x30) with the scope's own country; `add_core = this` means the scope's province with EventScope_GetCountryTag's country; `add_core = REB` (the text, case-sensitive) takes the scope's rebel faction's country.
addresses.evidence: Slot 7 decompiled, ret 0x104 at 0x59FE3A; Execute 0x99FE40 decompiled for how the two fields are used. One holder, CAddCoreEffect slot 7.

addresses.name: CRemCoreEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `remove_core`: the same double reading as CAddCoreEffect's, one dword later - tag into +0x24/+0x28, `atoi(text)` into +0x2C - because CRemCoreEffect is a CIntEffect and its +0x20 is the (unused) integer. Execute (0x5A06C0) resolves province and country exactly as add_core does and removes the core if present.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled, ret 0x104 at 0x9A06BA; Execute read. One holder.

addresses.name: CGovernmentEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `government`. In order: the text **exactly** `REB` (a byte compare, case-sensitive) sets +0x24 - Execute then takes the government of the scope's rebel faction; token `this` -> +0x1C (the THIS country's government); `from` -> +0x1D (the FROM country's); otherwise the government database by name (StringHashFind_At44, exact) into +0x20, **null on a miss with no message** - and Execute (0x5A1010) does nothing when it ends with a null government.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled, the REB literal read at 0x15BE948; ret 0x104. Execute decompiled. One holder.

addresses.name: CCoupEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `coup_by`: `this`/`from` set +0x1C/+0x1D, otherwise the **ideology** of that name (GetIdeologies + CNameDataBase::GetByName, exact) into +0x20, null and silent on a miss.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; three ret 0x104 exits. One holder.

addresses.name: CJoinFactionEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `join_faction`: FindFactionByName over the ideology database (exact, case-sensitive against CFaction +0xC, e.g. `axis`) into +0x20. **No this/from form** - the words are just names that match nothing. The `Unknown faction '<name>'.` log (effect.cpp line 0x39F) is behind a null test that **cannot fire**: FindFactionByName answers the CNullFaction on a miss, never null.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; ret 0x104 at 0x9A1C50. FindFactionByName's every exit read. One holder.

addresses.name: CLeaveFactionEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `leave_faction`: identical to CJoinFactionEffect's, its unreachable log on effect.cpp line 0x3BA.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; ret 0x104 at 0x9A21B0. One holder.

addresses.name: CRemoveModifierEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `remove_country_modifier` and `remove_province_modifier`: the static-modifier database by name (CTraitDataBase_Find over g_static_modifiers, exact) into +0x20; a miss logs `Unknown modifier-type '<name>'.` (effect.cpp line 0x470, channel 0x10004). No this/from.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; ret 0x104 at 0x9A4091. Held by the two CRemoveModifierEffect heirs only.

addresses.name: Effect_TakeStringValue
addresses.comment: Assign the value text to the Hoi3CString at +0x20, and nothing else - **no this/from handling**, so `set_country_flag = this` sets a flag literally named `this`. Slot 7 of the six flag effects (`set_/clr_` country, province, global) and of `change_province_name`. Left class-free (trap 4): CRenameProvinceEffect derives from CEffect, not from CFlagEffect, so the seven holders share no ancestor that declares slot 7 and the body is a fold of two identical sources.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: one std::string::assign; `ret 0x104` at 0x9A4968, six int3 before the entry. vtable.py --holding: 7 tables, all slot 7.

addresses.name: Effect_TakeCountryTagValue
addresses.comment: The tag reader of 18 keywords: token `this` sets +0x1C, `from` +0x1D, anything else is CCountryDataBase::GetTag(text) into the CCountryTag at +0x20/+0x24 - `---`/0 for an unknown tag, compared on the **first three characters, case-insensitively** (`_strnicmp`). It does not clear the flags first. Slot 7 of the eleven CCountryTargetEffect heirs (change_controller, create_alliance, create_vassal, end_guarantee, end_non_aggression_pact, end_war, guarantee, leave_alliance, military_access, end_military_access, non_aggression_pact) and the seven CDiplomaticEffect heirs (casus_belli, add_casus_belli, do_election, inherit, release, secede_province, surrender_inherit). Class-free (trap 4): the two middles are siblings under CEffect, so this is a fold.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; three ret 0x104 exits, the last at 0x9A7C23. vtable.py --holding: 18 tables, all slot 7, chains read from the RTTI export.

addresses.name: CAddSubUnitEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `<sub-unit type> = <where>` (CEffect::LoadKey default arm, step 7). Clears the flags, +0x20 and +0x28; token `this` -> +0x1C (Execute: THIS scope's province), `from` -> +0x1D (THIS scope's FROM province), `current` (1576) -> +0x28 (the scope's own province, **owned by its controller**); otherwise `atoi(text) * 1000` into +0x20, a province id. Execute (0x5A8440) adds the brigade to the owner's unit in that province with fewer than four regiments of the same arm, or makes a new unit.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; four ret 0x104 exits. Execute decompiled for the meaning of each flag. One holder.

addresses.name: CReleaseVassalEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `release_vassal`: `this`/`from` set +0x1C/+0x1D; token `random` (1558) sets +0x28; otherwise GetTag into +0x20/+0x24 - and **a tag the database does not know also sets +0x28**, so a misspelt tag behaves as `random` rather than as nothing. What Execute does with +0x28 (it resolves through 0x5AF510) was not read.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x9AEB20-0x9AEBE2: `cmp eax, 0x616; je 0x9aebd0` and, after GetTag, `test edx, edx; jne` past the same `mov byte ptr [esi+0x28], 1`. One holder.

addresses.name: CRemoveMinisterEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `remove_minister`. Token `yes` sets +0x24 and stops. Otherwise the text is looked up as a **government position** (GetByName) into +0x28; if that is a real position (its slot 14, `mov al,1` on CGovernmentPosition and false on CNullGovernmentPosition) it stops, and otherwise `atoi(text) * 1000` goes into +0x20 - a minister id. So `remove_minister = 2001` is a minister, `remove_minister = head_of_state` a post, `remove_minister = yes` the third form. No this/from.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x9B17BC-0x9B181C read after the decompiler mis-structured the string destructor: `call [eax+0x38]; test al,al; jne` past `atoi; imul eax,eax,0x3e8; mov [edi+0x20],eax`. CGovernmentPosition slot 14 is 0xA92590 (`mov al,1; ret`). One holder.

addresses.name: CStrategicResourceEffect::TakeScalarValue
addresses.comment: Slot 7 of `strategic_resource`: +0x20 starts as the null strategic resource; token `none` keeps it; anything else is the strategic-resource database by name (GetByName, exact) - and **a miss stores null, not the null resource**. No this/from.

addresses.name: RegisterCompiledTokens
addresses.comment: **Puts every compiled keyword into the lexer's ternary search tree** `g_dynamic_tokens` (rva 0x1310DF0): walks the CToken array g_save_tokens (VA 0x1A8CCA0, stride 0x104, to 0x1B14808) with a heap int of each id as the value. It first sets the container's staging flag (0x1710DF4), so each name goes through 0x44D8E0 into a sorted staging list (a case-sensitive memcmp order); then 0x747A00 clears the flag and inserts the staged names through TernarySearchTreeInsert - which **lowercases** every character - at 0x747A9F/0x747AFF. Then it sets the token table's built flag (0x1A857BC) and count (0x1A857B8, the highest id + 1). Together with TextTokenizer_NextToken's lowercasing lookup this is why **every keyword of the script language is case-insensitive** - `ADD_CORE`, `This` and `YES` are the tokens they look like. 0x669B80 to the bare `ret` at 0x669C9E. One caller (0x669B4C).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0xA69B80-0xA69C9E read: `mov byte ptr [0x1710df4], 1`, the loop's `cmp byte ptr [0x1710df4], 1; jne` choosing 0x44D8E0 over 0x44DA70, `add edi, 0x104; cmp edi, 0x1b14808; jl`, then `mov ecx, 0x1710dec; call 0x747a00`; 0x747A00 writes 0 to [esi+8] and calls 0x44DA70 twice; 0x44D8E0 read as a sorted-list insert of 0x24-byte nodes. Wrong if the TST at 0x1710DF0 were not the one TextTokenizer_NextToken searches (it is: `mov eax, 0x1710df0; call 0xa7e030` at 0xA6A586).

addresses.name: TextTokenizer_NextToken
addresses.comment: **Slot 1 of the text tokenizer (vftable 0x15FD1FC): one token off a script file**, the far end of every `LoadKey`. Answers 1, or 0 at end of input; the kind goes to +0xC and the text to +0x10. With +0x110 set it is a pushback. Skips white space, then by the first character: `#`, **`!` and `;` start a comment to the end of the line** (kind 9, then it recurses); `"` reads to the next quote and is **kind 0xF without any keyword lookup** - so a quoted `"yes"` or `"this"` is not the keyword; `=` 1, `{` 3, `}` 4, `(` 5, `)` 6, `,` 8. Otherwise a bare word runs to white space or one of `! " # ( ) , ; = { }` - `<`, `>` and `.` are ordinary characters. A word whose first character is a digit or `-` is **0xC (a number)** outright; any other word is looked up in g_dynamic_tokens with TernarySearchTreeFind (case-insensitive) and takes that token's id; failing that it is 0xC if it consists only of digits, `.` and `-`, and **0xF (an identifier)** otherwise. Consequence: a country tag spelled like a compiled token - `PAN` (317, `pan`) and `PHI` (81, `phi`) - never arrives as 0xF, so EventScopeSpec_Construct never looks it up as a tag.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0xA6A2E0-0xA6A5DB read; the punctuation classes decoded from the byte table at 0xA6A608 and the jump table at 0xA6A5E4 (lexclass.py in the wave scratchpad); the classification at 0xA6A56B-0xA6A5BF. Wrong if any bare-word path set 0xF before the TST lookup.

addresses.name: CRandomListEffect::Execute
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CRandomListEffect::Execute(CRandomListEffect* this, CEventScope* scope, int unused)
addresses.comment: `random_list`. Does nothing when the total weight (+0x20) is not positive. Otherwise two steps of the scope's LCG (`*0x343FD + 0x269EC3`, state written back to `scope +8`), `roll = ((r1 >> 16) & 0x7FFF) * ((r2 >> 16) & 0x7FFF) % total`, then walks the weights beside the children, subtracting each weight from the roll and **running the first entry for which the remainder is not positive** (its slot 11, with 0 as the second argument). So entry 1 takes rolls 0..w1 - one more than its weight - and the last entry one fewer than its weight; a first entry of weight 0 still fires on a roll of 0.

struct_fields.name: tag
struct_fields.comment: The faction's name - `axis`, `allies`, `comintern` style keys, **a std::string, not a CCountryTag**: the constructor (0x5224B0) initialises it as a string (`lea ecx,[esi+0xc]; mov [ecx+0x14], 0xf; mov [ecx+0x10], 0; mov byte ptr [ecx], 0; assign("")`), FindFactionByName compares it as one (size at +0x1C, capacity at +0x20, SSO buffer at +0xC), and the Lua registration is `CString const& GetTag(CFaction const&)` (luabind.json, Tag at 12, type CString). It reads live as four characters (`axis`, `alli`, `comi`) because a short string's characters sit at the start of the buffer. Saved as `tag`. 0xC + 0x1C = 0x28 = `Members`, so the string fills the gap exactly.
struct_fields.evidence: Three independent readings, all in the bytes: the constructor's string init, FindFactionByName's SSO test, and luabind's return type CString. Wrong if any reader of +0x10 treated it as an int id.
struct_fields.revises: type CCountryTag -> Hoi3CString; the old type came from BiceLib/GameClasses/CFaction.hpp:16 and luabind.json already says CString
